With some help from Lucy’s dad, they visit an 800-year-old oak tree and forage for ground ivy, a fragrant herb related to mint and sage. And there’s always time for a new basket. In Gaelic with English subtitles

Together, they share the joys and frustrations of birdwatching as well as the pure exhilaration in spotting a bird that means so much to them. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: The Latest Secrets of Hieroglyphs
programme.desc: The great history of Egypt is inscribed on its monuments, temples and tombs, but hieroglyphs – the written language of the ancient Egyptians – fell silent until 1822 when a young French scholar, Jean-François Champollion, became the first person to decipher their texts for over a thousand years. Champollion’s insights and the work of other scholars helped bring an entire civilisation back to life. Today, researchers are increasingly interested in the authors who created these hieroglyphic works. Near Luxor, we follow a new generation of Egyptologists as they unlock the texts inscribed inside a richly adorned tomb, revealing the beliefs and lives of the priests, scribes, painters, engravers and builders who created this grand funerary monument.

programme.desc: AI Decoded looks at the surprising alliance between Meta and Apple, which raises one of the biggest questions facing the AI industry. As technology companies invest hundreds of billions into ever-larger data centres, the two Silicon Valley rivals are backing a different vision: powerful AI models that can run locally on advanced desktop computers rather than relying entirely on the cloud. For years, bigger AI has meant bigger infrastructure. Vast data centres now consume enormous amounts of energy, water and land, while communities around the world are increasingly pushing back against their expansion. But what if there was another way? What if businesses could run powerful AI systems from their own offices, on machines sitting beneath their desks?
